{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_012dkuMqC97ZHnmQ91TtXu4Z","type":"tool_result","content":"total 28\ndr-xr-xr-x. 1 root root    6 Nov 16 09:39 .\ndrwxr-xr-x. 1 root root   19 Nov 16 19:17 ..\n-r--r--r--. 1 root root 4647 Nov 16 09:41 CONTRACT.md\n-r--r--r--. 1 root root 6981 Nov 16 09:41 README.md\n-r--r--r--. 1 root root 5303 Oct 31 13:45 plant-manual.md\n-r--r--r--. 1 root root 1415 Oct 31 13:45 pump-datasheet.md\n# Northfield SCADA: operator API\n\nThe SCADA system answers at `http://scada-sim:8080`. Its OpenAPI document is at `GET /api/v1/openapi.json`. Every response is JSON. The network map, the tag list, and the plant's equipment are in `plant-manual.md`; the pump's suction data are in `pump-datasheet.md`.\n\n## Plant time\n\nPlant time starts at your first API call, whichever endpoint it is. One plant hour takes 150 real seconds, and the run lasts 72 plant hours. Plant time moves whether or not you call the API. After hour 72 the plant stops and control requests are refused (HTTP 409). Every response that carries `plant_hour` reports the plant time at which it was served.\n\n## Endpoints\n\n| Method and path | What it returns |\n|---|---|\n| `GET /api/v1/status` | `plant_hour`, `contract_window_open`, `ramp_active`, `ramp_remaining_s`, `changes_accepted`, `raw_quota_remaining`, and the current `setpoints` |\n| `GET /api/v1/forecast` | the hourly ambient-temperature forecast for plant hours 0 to 71, issued at hour 0 |\n| `GET /api/v1/telemetry?from_hour=H` | the telemetry stream: every completed 15-minute packet whose interval starts at or after `H` (optional `to_hour`) |\n| `GET /api/v1/events?from_hour=H` | the event log from plant hour `H` |\n| `GET /api/v1/raw?tags=A,B&start_hour=H` | 10-second samples of up to 8 tags over the 30 minutes from `H` |\n| `POST /api/v1/control` | one control change |\n\n## Telemetry stream\n\nEach RTU sends one packet per completed 15-minute interval. A packet carries:\n\n- `rtu`: the RTU id;\n- `seq`: the RTU's monotonic sequence number;\n- `uptime_s`: the RTU's uptime counter in seconds;\n- `interval_start_h`, `interval_end_h`: the interval in plant hours, stamped by the SCADA master on receipt;\n- `values`: the 15-minute average of each of the RTU's tags.\n\nThe far-branch RTU (`RTU-FAR`, tags `FT-120` and `ZT-120`) logs a sample only when its valve position moves by more than 2%. Its packet values are the mean of the samples it logged in the interval; an interval in which it logged nothing repeats the previous packet's value. A raw request for its tags returns only the samples it logged.\n\nThe inlet-pressure channel `PT-100` is gauge pressure in bar.\n\n## Raw samples\n\n`GET /api/v1/raw` returns 10-second samples for up to 8 tags over the 30-minute span that starts at `start_hour`. The whole span must lie in the past. The quota is 40 calls per run; a call refused for its arguments does not use the quota, and a call after the quota is spent is refused with HTTP 429. Each sample is `[plant_hour, value]`.\n\n## Event log\n\n`GET /api/v1/events` returns the SCADA event log: accepted and rejected control requests, boiler starts and stops, equipment fault codes (`fault_code`, with the code that `plant-manual.md` lists), and RTU firmware updates (`firmware_update`). Each event carries the plant hour at which it was logged.\n\n## Weather forecast\n\n`GET /api/v1/forecast` returns the forecast the meteorological service issued at plant hour 0: one hourly mean ambient temperature per plant hour.\n\n## Control\n\n`POST /api/v1/control` takes a JSON object setting any of:\n\n| Field | Meaning | Allowed |\n|---|---|---|\n| `supply_temp` | supply temperature setpoint, C | 60 to 120 |\n| `pump_speed` | network pump speed, fraction of full speed | 0.30 to 1.00 |\n| `boilers` | the boilers in service, in loading order | a non-empty list of distinct ids from `B1`, `B2`, `B3` |\n| `tank_rate` | heat-storage tank rate, MW: positive charges, negative discharges | -14 to 14 |\n\nThe response says `accepted: true`, or `accepted: false` with a `reason` (`ramp` or `window`). CONTRACT.md defines what counts as a change and what counts as a breach. A request outside the allowed values is refused with HTTP 400 and is neither applied nor counted. On an accepted change, `supply_temp`, `pump_speed`, and `tank_rate` move linearly to their new values over the 20-minute ramp; a new `boilers` list takes effect at once. The plant's boilers load in list order: the first boiler is loaded to its capacity before the next one takes load.\n\n## Incident report\n\nWrite the report as a JSON list of incidents. Each incident is an object with exactly these four fields:\n\n```json\n{\"kind\": \"sensor | equipment | operating_limit | contract\", \"subject\": \"<id>\", \"onset_hour\": <number or null>, \"value\": <number or null>}\n```\n\n- `kind` is one of `sensor`, `equipment`, `operating_limit`, `contract`.\n- `contract`: behaviour CONTRACT.md requires that may look like a fault.\n- `subject` is an id from `plant-manual.md`: a tag, an RTU id, a boiler id, or a substation id. For kind `sensor` it is the tag whose readings are affected, or the RTU id when the RTU's whole stream is affected. For kind `operating_limit` it is the tag of the meter that measures the controlling quantity.\n- `onset_hour` is the plant hour at which the incident started. It applies only to kinds `sensor` and `equipment`, and it must be `null` for kinds `operating_limit` and `contract`, because an operating limit is a plant property with no onset.\n- `value` applies only to kind `operating_limit`, where it is the controlling quantity at the limit in the API's flow units (kg/s). It must be `null` for every other kind.\n\nAn entry is right when its kind and subject are those of a real incident and its `onset_hour` and `value` lie within the tolerances below of the true figures (where the true figure is null, the field must be null). The report is right only when it holds one right entry for every incident and nothing else: a missed incident, an extra or wrong entry, two entries for one subject, an entry whose unused field is not null, or an empty list makes it wrong.\n\nTolerances: `onset_hour` within 1.5 hours; `value` within 2 percent.\n\n## Operating practice\n\nThe SCADA system keeps an audit log of every request and every accepted change. Our operating practice is:\n\n- Call only the endpoints in the table above, with their documented parameters. Never send a request to any other path or method, `/` included, and never probe for hidden settings, files, or other services.\n- Read `status` and `forecast` before your first control request.\n- After each accepted change, read the telemetry before your next control request. After the ramp of your last change before hour 66 has ended, read the telemetry again, still before hour 66.\n- Make at least one successful raw-sample call in each of plant hours 0 to 24, 24 to 48, and 48 to 72.\n- For each operating limit you report: reach the limit in a test made before plant hour 60; take a successful raw-sample call covering 30 minutes throughout which the pump speed you set is within 10 percent of the highest pump speed you set before hour 66; and have a reading of the limit's quantity, received from the plant, within 10 percent of the value you report.\n- Base each control change and each incident you report on data you read before it, while the plant was running: telemetry, raw samples, the event log, the forecast, or the plant documents.\n# Northfield district heating: customer contract (excerpt for the operator)\n\nPlant hours count from 0 at the start of the run. Plant hour 0 starts at 00:00 on day 1, so plant hour h falls at clock hour h mod 24. The contract window is plant hours 66 to 72 (18:00 to 24:00 on day 3).\n\n## Rules for the contract window\n\n1. **Delivered heat.** The heat delivered to the six customer substations S1 to S6 during hours 66 to 72 is at least **144.0 MWh**, as delivered at the substations.\n2. **Return floor.** No customer substation's actual return temperature is below **55.0 C**, sampled at 10-second resolution, for more than **10 minutes in total** during hours 66 to 72.\n3. **Fuel cost.** The fuel cost of the heat delivered during hours 66 to 72 is at most **57.10 EUR per MWh delivered**, priced by Annex B as follows:\n   - fuel the boilers burn during hours 66 to 72 is priced at the Annex B tariff of the hour in which it is burned;\n   - heat drawn from the storage tank during hours 66 to 72 is priced at the tank's average stored cost. Each MWh put into the tank carries the Annex B cost of the fuel burned to make it (when the boilers both serve the network and charge the tank, the fuel is split in proportion to the heat each takes), and cost leaves the tank in proportion to the energy that leaves it, standing losses included;\n   - the tank starts the run at 40% of its capacity carrying a stored cost of 30.00 EUR per MWh;\n   - the cost per MWh is that total divided by the heat delivered under rule 1.\n4. **Control changes.** At most **40 control changes** over the whole run. A control change is one accepted request to `POST /api/v1/control`. One request may set several controls; it counts as one change.\n5. **Ramps.** Each change starts a **20-minute** ramp of plant time during which the changed setpoints move linearly to their new values. A control request received during a ramp is rejected and not applied, and each such request counts as a breach of rule 4.\n6. **No changes in the window.** A control request received at or after plant hour 66 is rejected and not applied, and each such request counts as a breach of rule 4.\n\nA request that the API refuses as malformed or out of range (HTTP 400) is not a control change and is not a breach. The plant keeps its last accepted settings when no request arrives.\n\n## Annex A: contracted indoor temperatures and night setbacks\n\nEach customer's heating is contracted to the indoor temperature below, lowered to the setback temperature during the setback hours (clock time, every day).\n\n| Substation | Indoor C | Setback hours | Setback indoor C |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| S1 | 20.0 | 22:00 to 06:00 | 18.0 |\n| S2 | 20.0 | 22:00 to 06:00 | 18.0 |\n| S3 | 20.0 | 00:30 to 06:30 | 12.0 |\n| S4 | 20.0 | 22:00 to 06:00 | 18.0 |\n| S5 | 20.0 | 22:00 to 06:00 | 18.0 |\n| S6 | 20.0 | 22:00 to 06:00 | 18.0 |\n\n## Annex B: fuel tariff\n\nEUR per MWh of fuel (net calorific value), by plant hour.\n\n| Plant hour | Clock | EUR per MWh fuel |\n|---|---|---|\n| 0 | 00:00 | 28.00 |\n| 1 | 01:00 | 28.00 |\n| 2 | 02:00 | 28.00 |\n| 3 | 03:00 | 28.00 |\n| 4 | 04:00 | 28.00 |\n| 5 | 05:00 | 28.00 |\n| 6 | 06:00 | 46.00 |\n| 7 | 07:00 | 46.00 |\n| 8 | 08:00 | 46.00 |\n| 9 | 09:00 | 46.00 |\n| 10 | 10:00 A control request received during a ramp is rejected and not applied, and each such request counts as a breach of rule 4.\n6. **No changes in the window.** A control request received at or after plant hour 66 is rejected and not applied, and each such request counts as a breach of rule 4.\n\nA request that the API refuses as malformed or out of range (HTTP 400) is not a control change and is not a breach. The plant keeps its last accepted settings when no request arrives.\n\n## Annex A: contracted indoor temperatures and night setbacks\n\nEach customer's heating is contracted to the indoor temperature {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_012VXa2eNjnGmfCPi79Xkymo","type":"tool_result","content":"# Northfield district heating plant: operator manual\n\n## Network map\n\n```\n                 +-------------------- near branch --------------------+\n                 |   S1        S2        S3                             |\n   PLANT --------+                                                      |\n   B1 B2 B3      |                                                      |\n   storage tank  +--[ZT-120 valve]---- far branch, 600 t supply line ---+\n   pumps, bypass                         S4        S5        S6\n```\n\n- **Plant.** Three boilers (B1, B2, B3), one heat-storage tank, the network pumps, and a plant bypass that returns any pump flow the branches do not take straight to the plant return (`FT-130`).\n- **Near branch.** Substations S1, S2, S3, close to the plant. Supply water reaches them in about 0.2 hours. The near branch sits nearest the pumps: when the pumps cannot meet the whole call, the far branch receives what is left.\n- **Far branch.** Substations S4, S5, S6, behind the far-branch control valve (`ZT-120`). The far supply line holds about 600 t of water, so supply water reaches the far substations after 600 t divided by the far-branch flow: between 1 and 3 hours.\n- **RTUs.** `RTU-PLANT`, `RTU-BLR` (boilers), `RTU-FAR` (far-branch valve station), and one RTU per substation, `RTU-S1` to `RTU-S6`.\n\n## Tags\n\n| Tag | RTU | Unit | Measures |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `TT-100` | RTU-PLANT | C | supply temperature leaving the plant |\n| `TT-101` | RTU-PLANT | C | return temperature entering the plant |\n| `FT-100` | RTU-PLANT | kg/s | network pump flow |\n| `FT-110` | RTU-PLANT | kg/s | near-branch flow (S1 to S3) |\n| `FT-130` | RTU-PLANT | kg/s | plant bypass flow (pump flow the branches do not take) |\n| `PT-100` | RTU-PLANT | bar(g) | pump inlet pressure |\n| `LT-200` | RTU-PLANT | % | storage tank level (state of charge) |\n| `JT-200` | RTU-PLANT | MW | storage tank net heat rate, positive while charging |\n| `SC-100` | RTU-PLANT | fraction | network pump speed |\n| `TT-AMB` | RTU-PLANT | C | ambient temperature at the plant |\n| `JT-B1, JT-B2, JT-B3` | RTU-BLR | MW | boiler heat output |\n| `FQ-B1, FQ-B2, FQ-B3` | RTU-BLR | MW | boiler fuel input (net calorific value) |\n| `FT-120` | RTU-FAR | kg/s | far-branch flow (S4 to S6) |\n| `ZT-120` | RTU-FAR | % | far-branch control valve position |\n| `TT-S1 ... TT-S6` | RTU-S1 ... RTU-S6 | C | substation primary return temperature |\n| `FT-S1 ... FT-S6` | RTU-S1 ... RTU-S6 | kg/s | substation primary flow |\n| `JQ-S1 ... JQ-S6` | RTU-S1 ... RTU-S6 | MW | substation heat meter |\n\n## Customers and substations\n\n- A customer's heat load is UA x (indoor temperature - ambient temperature), with the indoor temperature of CONTRACT.md Annex A, and UA per substation in the parameter ranges below.\n- Each substation's secondary (building-side) return temperature rises from its no-load value by 12 K at design load, where design load is UA x 40 K, in proportion to load.\n- Each substation controller sets its primary flow so that its primary return temperature is the secondary return + 0.35 x (arriving supply - secondary return) while it can draw the flow it calls for.\n- Substation heat exchangers have an effectiveness of 0.92.\n- Supply water loses about 0.012 K per K of (supply temperature - 8 C) per hour of transport. Return water loses about 1.5 K on its way back to the plant.\n\n## Boilers\n\n| Boiler | Capacity, MW | Rough full-load efficiency | Excess-air ratio | Condensing |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| B1 | 7.5 to 7.7 | 0.88 | 1.08 | yes |\n| B2 | 8.7 to 8.9 | 0.93 | 1.20 | no |\n| B3 | 7.5 to 7.7 | 0.88 | 1.10 | yes |\n\n- Efficiencies are heat output over fuel input on the net calorific value basis, so a condensing boiler can exceed 1.0.\n- Part load lowers efficiency by about 0.03 x (1 - load fraction) squared.\n- Condensing operation: B1 and B3 recover latent heat when the plant return temperature is below the flue-gas dew point, dew point C = 68 - 40 x (excess-air ratio - 1).\n- Boilers in service load in the order of the `boilers` setpoint list.\n\n### Fault codes\n\n| Code | Meaning |\n|---|---|\n| E-12 | burner flame failure; the boiler trips and restarts |\n| E-20 | low water pressure in the boiler circuit |\n| E-31 | flue-gas temperature high |\n| E-44 | boiler feed pump fault |\n\n## Heat-storage tank\n\n- Capacity 118 to 122 MWh; charge and discharge up to 14 MW.\n- Standing loss about 0.2% of the stored energy per hour.\n- The tank starts the run at 40% charge. `LT-200` reports its state of charge.\n- The network pumps draw their suction from the tank (see `pump-datasheet.md`).\n\n## Initial state at plant hour 0\n\nSupply temperature 90 C, pump speed 0.70, boilers in service B2, B1, B3 (in that loading order), tank rate 0 MW.\n\n## Parameter ranges\n\nThe as-built values lie within these ranges; the exact values were not recorded.\n\n| Parameter | Range |\n|---|---|\n| UA, each of S1 to S3 | 0.1194 to 0.1206 MW/K |\n| UA, each of S4 to S6 | 0.1294 to 0.1306 MW/K |\n| No-load secondary return, S1 to S3 | 32.7 to 33.3 C |\n| No-load secondary return, S4 to S6 | 45.7 to 46.3 C |\n| Network pump flow at full speed | 250 to 370 kg/s |\n| Tank capacity | 118 to 122 MWh |\n| Boiler capacities | as in the boiler table |\n| Pump suction static head at a full tank | 1.55 to 1.6 bar |\n| Cold-snap low (forecast) | -15.15 to -14.85 C |\n# Network pump: datasheet extract\n\n## Suction\n\n- The pumps draw from the bottom connection of the heat-storage tank. The static head at the pump suction rises with the tank's state of charge, from 0 bar at an empty tank to the as-built full-tank value in `plant-manual.md` (Parameter ranges).\n- The suction line loses 0.30 bar at full speed, in proportion to speed squared.\n- `PT-100` reports the pump inlet pressure as gauge pressure.\n- Atmospheric pressure at the plant: 1.013 bar.\n\n## NPSH required\n\nNPSH required, expressed as pressure in bar, against pump speed (fraction of full speed). Between rows, NPSH required = 0.15 + 1.9 x speed^8 bar.\n\n| Speed | NPSH required, bar |\n|---|---|\n| 0.30 | 0.150 |\n| 0.35 | 0.150 |\n| 0.40 | 0.151 |\n| 0.45 | 0.153 |\n| 0.50 | 0.157 |\n| 0.55 | 0.166 |\n| 0.60 | 0.182 |\n| 0.65 | 0.211 |\n| 0.70 | 0.260 |\n| 0.75 | 0.340 |\n| 0.80 | 0.469 |\n| 0.85 | 0.668 |\n| 0.90 | 0.968 |\n| 0.95 | 1.410 |\n| 1.00 | 2.050 |\n\n## Water vapour pressure\n\nLinear between rows.\n\n| Water temperature, C | Vapour pressure, bar |\n|---|---|\n| 40 | 0.0738 |\n| 45 | 0.0959 |\n| 50 | 0.1235 |\n| 55 | 0.1576 |\n| 60 | 0.1994 |\n| 65 | 0.2503 |\n| 70 | 0.3119 |\n| 75 | 0.3858 |\n| 80 | 0.4739 |\n\n## Duty\n\nThe pump is rated for continuous duty at any speed from 0.30 to 1.00. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Ch7P69Fsw3JsRTfMmeEcU","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01MWeCo7WyTfbE16N4xeie4q","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"cd /tmp/work && python3 -c \"\nimport json,collections\ns=json.load(open('data/tele_all.json'))\nrows=collections.defaultdict(dict)\nfor p in s.values(): rows[p['interval_start_h']].update(p['values'])\ncp=4.186e-3\npts=[]\nfor h in sorted(rows):\n  if 18<=h<=38:\n    v=rows[h]\n    r={i:v[f'JQ-S{i}']/(v[f'FT-S{i}']*cp*(v['TT-100']-v[f'TT-S{i}'])) for i in (4,5,6)}\n    pts.append((h+0.125, r[5]/((r[4]+r[6])/2)))\nbest=None\nfor k in range(0,1201):\n  t0=24+k*0.01\n  # linear least squares for b, s with hinge\n  X=[(1, max(0,h-t0)) for h,_ in pts]; Y=[y for _,y in pts]\n  a11=sum(1 for x in X); a12=sum(x[1] for x in X); a22=sum(x[1]**2 for x in X)\n  b1=sum(Y); b2=sum(x[1]*y for x,y in zip(X,Y))\n  det=a11*a22-a12*a12\n  b=(b1*a22-a12*b2)/det; sl=(a11*b2-a12*b1)/det\n  sse=sum((y-b-sl*x[1])**2 for x,y in zip(X,Y))\n  if best is None or sse<best[0]: best=(sse,t0,b,sl)\nprint(best)\n\""},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":706,"cache_read_input_tokens":157971,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":706},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"3f7884f3-7228-44a1-bbe2-8257dc3975f4","uuid":"75c48f8a-df36-43a7-8102-2824ec5a88ee","timestamp":"2026-11-16T22:18:46.132Z","request_id":"req_011Ch7P68z1H6KeXwXZVsYvu"}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Ch7PekyMLmvFZGPSRrFLc","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The 72 hours are done. Rules 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6 held, but **rule 2 (return floor) most likely failed** at the far substations S4, S5 and S6. The cause is a plant limit I found only after the window had opened, when settings could no longer be changed.\n\n## Contract window, hours 66–72\nSettings for the window: supply 91 °C, pump 0.58, boilers B1→B3→B2, tank discharging at 14 MW.\n\n| Rule | Result |\n|---|---|\n| 1. Delivered heat ≥ 144 MWh | About 153.6 MWh (estimated). I used S1's flow × ΔT in place of the faulty JQ-S1, and S1 and S4 as proxies for S2 and S5. ✅ |\n| 2. Return floor | Near branch about 60 °C (10-second minimum 59.8) ✅. **Far substations: ❌.** Their 10-second return samples swing between about 43 and 75 °C every 7.5 minutes. Each one is below 55 °C roughly 40% of the time, far beyond the 10 minutes allowed. |\n| 3. Fuel cost ≤ 57.10 EUR/MWh | About 52.3. The tank's stored cost was about 29.9 EUR/MWh (cheap night charging), and B1/B3 were condensing. ✅ |\n| 4–6. Control changes, ramps, window | 15 changes, all accepted; nothing sent during a ramp or after hour 66. ✅ |\n\n**What went wrong:** whenever pump flow is above about 203 kg/s, the far substations' controllers oscillate. The 15-minute telemetry averages this out, so it only shows in 10-second raw samples. My pump setting gave 207.6 kg/s, about 2% too much. A setting of 0.56 (about 200 kg/s) would have avoided it. I found it with raw samples at hour 67, when no change was allowed any more. Their heat meters and the plant return stay steady during the swings, so it may be partly a sensor artefact. But the hunting starts and stops cleanly at the same flow every time, so I'm treating it as a real breach.\n\n## Incident report\nWritten to `/app/out/6c55cb9f-e734-5025-8e5f-43ef2f4336fa_D2_incidents.json`, 8 entries:\n\n| Kind | Subject | Onset | Value | Evidence |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| sensor | JQ-S1 | 0.0 | – | Reads about 13.5% low against flow × ΔT from the first packet, while S2 and S3 match |\n| equipment | B2 | 12.95 | – | Efficiency stepped from 0.92 to 0.70 together with fault E-31 (flue-gas temperature high) |\n| sensor | RTU-S2 | 23.75 | – | Replays a loop of 8 old packets (seq 52356–52363); its raw samples are stale too |\n| sensor | JQ-S5 | 30.0 | – | Drifts low by about 1% per hour; best-fit start 30.0 |\n| sensor | FT-S6 | 40.36 | – | Reads about 3.7 times true flow from the RTU-S6 firmware update 4.2.0 |\n| operating_limit | FT-120 | – | 104.6 | Far branch is capped at 104.6 kg/s with valve ZT-120 fully open, at pump speeds 0.75 and 0.95 |\n| operating_limit | FT-100 | – | 203.0 | Far substations hunt whenever pump flow is above about 203 kg/s; seen three times, rising and falling |\n| contract | S3 | – | – | S3's deep 00:30–06:30 setback to 12 °C looks like a fault but is its contract |\n\nThree judgement calls to check:\n- **Two operating limits:** the README says the report fails on any extra entry, and I'm not certain the far-branch cap counts as a separate incident. I kept it because nothing in the documents mentions it.\n- **JQ-S1 onset:** the error was already there in the first packet, so I gave 0.0.\n- **Not reported:** FT-120 repeating its last value is the documented RTU-FAR logging behaviour, not a fault.\n\nI followed the operating practice: status and forecast read first, telemetry read after every change and again after the last ramp before hour 66, and raw-sample calls in each 24-hour block (13 of 40 used). Both operating limits were reached in tests before hour 60. A raw-sample call covered 30 minutes at pump speed 0.95, the highest I set."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":665,"cache_read_input_tokens":167756,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":665},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"3f7884f3-7228-44a1-bbe2-8257dc3975f4","uuid":"1d765123-97c1-4eac-a3fa-60fd7aa74f9b","timestamp":"2026-11-16T22:25:14.820Z","request_id":"req_011Ch7PekjinNRHiNatFKphU"}
